evidence.era_dress: 5 figures (count copied from seed, not scored): (1) brown corduroy blazer + grey button shirt + tan trousers + brown shoes; (2) tan cardigan open over blue collared shirt + brown skirt + brown flats; (3) grey suit jacket + white shirt + red tie + dark brown trousers + black shoes; (4) green sweater vest over dark-green blouse + black skirt + black flats; (5) mustard turtleneck sweater + blue jeans + brown shoes. Inspected each figure at 2x crop: no lettering, logos, badges, or brand marks anywhere (buttons, cuffs, shoes, tie all plain). No Victorian holdovers survived the restyle -- no bonnets, top hats, shawls, breeches, high collars, or bustled/leg-of-mutton silhouettes; all five read as ordinary plain-cut 1980s workplace basics (blazer+trousers, cardigan+skirt, suit+tie, sweater-vest+skirt, sweater+jeans). Palette is muted throughout (browns, tans, grey, blue, dark green, black, mustard) with no saturated or era-anachronistic prints.
evidence.head_tones: Pixel-sampled the cheek/forehead of each figure via a throwaway script (deleted after use). Figures 1 and 4 sample (247,235,211)/(247,235,209), dist ~4-5 from #f5ead6 (245,234,214). Figures 2 and 5 sample (224,181,136)/(225,181,136), dist ~5 from #e2b78c (226,183,140). Figure 3 samples a flat, shading-uniform (139,94,63) across the whole face (verified with a 200x140px histogram -- single dominant color, no shadow/highlight variant), dist ~24-29 from #7a4f33 (122,79,51) -- notably looser than the other two tones' <6 fit, and looser than the ~20 outlier the r2 round already accepted, but still unambiguously closer to tone C than to A or B by a wide margin (next-closest tone is >100 away). Net: exactly 3 tones present, split 2-2-1, no fourth tone invented, not uniform.
evidence.hair_silhouettes: Cropped and enlarged each head. Figures 1 and 5: short, side-parted brown hair with a swept fringe -- same silhouette, near-identical. Figures 2 and 4: hair pinned/rolled up into a voluminous side-swept updo with curls gathered at the back -- same silhouette, brown vs blonde colour only. Figure 3: short curly cap (black, tight rounded curls close to the scalp). Exactly 3 silhouettes across 5 figures (2-2-1), all within the named catalog (short side-parted / short curly cap / hair pinned up); no fourth shape invented.
evidence.anchor_not_uniform: 3 distinct head tones (2-2-1), 3 distinct hair silhouettes (2-2-1), and 5 different full outfits spanning brown/tan/grey/blue/dark-green/black/mustard on the shared crowd-rig body and flat dot-eye/flat-mouth face. No two figures are visually interchangeable. Reads as a varied anonymous crowd, not clones.

crowd-exemplar-reroll-r3-candidate.notes: One borderline call: head_tones on figure 3. Its sampled color (139,94,63) is a flat, internally consistent fill (confirmed via histogram, not sampling noise) but sits dist ~24-29 from canonical #7a4f33 -- worse than this frame's other two tones (~4-6) and worse than the ~20 outlier r2 already tolerated. I'm passing it because neither of the axis's stated failure conditions is tripped (it is not a 4th invented tone -- next-closest canonical tone is >100 away, and the group is not uniform), but the drift is the largest seen across rounds so far and is worth a second look before this candidate is adopted as the standing anchor: if promoted, downstream seeded generations will inherit this slightly-lighter/warmer dark tone rather than the exact hex. era_dress and hair_silhouettes are clean passes with no ambiguity -- no lettering/logos/Victorian holdovers found on close inspection of all 5 figures, and the 3 hair shapes repeat cleanly in a 2-2-1 split. anchor_not_uniform is a clean pass on the combined tone/hair/outfit variation.
